case: UN Security Council ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida sanctions list: listing QDi.317 (2013) and delisting by Resolution 2799 (2025)
type: UN Security Council targeted sanctions (asset freeze, travel ban, arms embargo); al-Sharaa as listed individual
description: In July 2013 the Security Council's Al-Qaida sanctions committee (resolutions 1267/1989) added 'Abu Mohammed al-Jawlani', leader of the Nusra Front, to its sanctions list under reference QDi.317, subjecting him to an asset freeze and travel ban; the entry was later amended to his birth name, Ahmad Hussain al-Sharaa. According to UN News, the Nusra Front/HTS itself had been under UN sanctions since 2014. After he became president, the United States sponsored a resolution to remove him and Interior Minister Anas Khattab (QDi.336) from the list, welcoming the transitional government's commitments on humanitarian access, counter-terrorism and human rights.
outcome: Delisted. On 6 November 2025 the Security Council adopted Resolution 2799 (2025), which 'decides that Ahmed al-Sharaa, included on the ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida Sanctions List as Ahmad Hussain Al-Sharaa (QDi.317), and Anas Hasan Khattab (QDi.336) are delisted', by 14 votes in favour with China abstaining. China said the United States had forced action despite 'huge differences' among members; the United States called it a 'strong political signal' that Syria was in a new era. An EU spokesperson said the decision would be reflected in EU measures.
court: UN Security Council; ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida Sanctions Committee (resolutions 1267 (1999), 1989 (2011) and 2253 (2015))
presumption_note: A UN sanctions listing is a preventive administrative measure decided by a Security Council committee, not a criminal charge or conviction; no court ruled on the grounds for the listing, and al-Sharaa was delisted in November 2025.
key_facts: Resolution 2799 adopted on 6 November 2025: 14 in favour, China abstaining
Interior Minister Anas Khattab delisted at the same time

case: US designation of 'Muhammad al-Jawlani' as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist (2013) and its revocation (2025)
type: US terrorism designation under Executive Order 13224 (asset blocking); al-Sharaa as designated individual
description: On 16 May 2013 the US State Department designated Nusra Front leader Muhammad al-Jawlani a Specially Designated Global Terrorist under Executive Order 13224, blocking any property under US jurisdiction and generally prohibiting transactions with him. The department said he had been tasked by al-Qaida in Iraq with overthrowing the Syrian government and that Nusra suicide attacks under his leadership had killed civilians. The designation, with the US $10 million reward offered in 2017 (withdrawn in December 2024, see polemics), remained in force after he became president.
outcome: Revoked. Secretary of State Marco Rubio signed the revocation on 7 November 2025 (Public Notice 12876, published in the Federal Register on 1 December 2025), covering the alias Ahmed al-Sharaa, and the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control removed him and Anas Khattab from its sanctions list the same day. The State Department cited 'the progress demonstrated by the Syrian leadership after the departure of Bashar al-Assad'.
court: US Department of State (Secretary of State), with the Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC)
presumption_note: An executive terrorism designation is an administrative sanction, not a criminal charge; al-Sharaa was never indicted or tried in the United States, and the designation was revoked in November 2025.
key_facts: 7 November 2025: revocation signed; OFAC delisting announced the same day
The revocation followed the UN delisting by one day

case: United Kingdom asset freeze under the ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida sanctions regime (removed 2025)
type: UK financial sanctions (asset freeze) implementing the UN listing; al-Sharaa as designated individual
description: The United Kingdom applied the UN listing of al-Sharaa (UN reference QDi.317) through its ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida sanctions regime; after Brexit he was designated under the ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 (UK sanctions list reference AQD0115, OFSI group ID 12883), which froze any funds or economic resources he held under UK jurisdiction.
outcome: Removed. On 7 November 2025, after the Security Council's decision, the UK's Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation announced that Ahmad Hussain al-Sharaa and Anas Hasan Khattab had been removed from the UK sanctions list and were no longer subject to an asset freeze (notice mirrored by the Guernsey Financial Services Commission; reported by SANA).
court: HM Treasury, Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI), and the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office
presumption_note: An asset freeze implementing a UN listing is an administrative measure, not a criminal charge or conviction; no UK court ruled on the allegations, and the measure was lifted in November 2025.
key_facts: UK sanctions list reference AQD0115; OFSI ID 12883; UN reference QDi.317
7 November 2025: removed from the UK sanctions list

case: Reported Iraqi arrest warrant on terrorism charges
type: arrest warrant (al-Sharaa as suspect); reported, not executed
description: In April 2025, when Iraq invited al-Sharaa to the Arab League summit in Baghdad, Mustafa Sand, an MP from the Iran-aligned Coordination Framework, said the Supreme Judicial Council had confirmed to the foreign ministry that a valid arrest warrant had been issued against him, and an Iraqi security official confirmed the existence of the warrant to the Associated Press. According to AP, it concerns terrorism charges linked to his time with al-Qaeda insurgents fighting US forces in Iraq after 2003. The issuing court, the date and the precise charges have not been made public.
outcome: No arrest attempt or court proceeding has been reported. Al-Sharaa did not attend the 17 May 2025 summit, sending Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani, after objections from Iraqi Shiite factions; Iraqi security sources said the warrant remained in place but might not be enforced. No public update on the warrant's status had been found as of October 2026.
court: Iraqi judiciary (existence confirmed by the Supreme Judicial Council according to an Iraqi MP; issuing court not publicly identified)
presumption_note: Al-Sharaa has not been charged before or tried by any court in Iraq; the warrant's existence rests on statements by an MP and an anonymous security official, and he is presumed innocent.
key_facts: April 2025: warrant's existence reported by AP from an Iraqi MP and a security official
May 2025: al-Sharaa skipped the Baghdad Arab League summit
No enforcement or proceeding reported as of October 2026

case: Criminal complaint by the Kurdish Community of Germany (KGD) to the Federal Prosecutor General
type: criminal complaint (Strafanzeige) naming al-Sharaa as suspect; investigation declined
description: In early November 2025 Mehmet Tanriverdi, deputy chairman of the Kurdish Community of Germany (KGD), filed a criminal complaint with the Federal Prosecutor General in Karlsruhe accusing al-Sharaa of genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and forming, leading or supporting a terrorist organisation; the KGD said he bore joint responsibility for the 2014 genocide of Yazidi Kurds and for violence against minorities in Syria and Iraq. German prosecutors confirmed receipt of the complaint to AFP on 10 November 2025. Al-Sharaa did not respond publicly to the complaint in the sources consulted.
outcome: In a letter to the KGD dated 5 January 2026, signed by Senior Prosecutor Anna Zabeck, the Federal Prosecutor General declined to open an investigation because of al-Sharaa's 'unrestricted personal immunity' as serving head of state of Syria: under section 20(2) of the Courts Constitution Act he is not subject to German jurisdiction, and any police or prosecution inquiry is inadmissible whether or not he is in Germany (RND, reported by the Berliner Zeitung). The decision rests on immunity and does not assess the allegations.
court: Federal Prosecutor General at the Federal Court of Justice (Generalbundesanwalt beim Bundesgerichtshof), Karlsruhe
presumption_note: No investigation was opened and no charge was brought; the prosecutor's refusal was based on head-of-state immunity, not on the merits. Al-Sharaa is presumed innocent of the acts alleged in the complaint.
key_facts: Complaint filed in early November 2025; confirmed to AFP on 10 November 2025
5 January 2026: investigation declined on grounds of personal immunity (§ 20(2) GVG)
